data.title: Apple's Next Legal Risk Could Reach $40 Billion
data.description:
Apple Inc. (AAPL, Financials), the creator of the iPhone, is headed for a jury trial in a biometric privacy issue that might become one of its biggest legal concerns.

A federal court in Illinois decided to dismiss most accusations that Apple's Photos app collects and saves facial faceprints without sufficient notice or consent.

The plaintiffs believe that nearly 8 million Illinois citizens are in the certified class.

Penalties can be as high as $5,000 per person for breaches of the state's biometric privacy statute that are willful or negligent. This might result in a possible exposure of up to $40 billion.

That doesn't imply Apple will end up paying anywhere close to that amount.

The corporation disputes any wrongdoing, saying its facial-recognition technology does not make the type of regulated biometric scan that the law covers.

But the potential enormity of the liability makes it a hard case to dismiss.

That matters beyond Apple too. Such arguments over face data might spill over from the internet giant to other big tech corporations as courts figure out how decades-old privacy regulations relate to modern AI-driven recognition techniques.

The crucial question for investors is whether the case remains small or sets a larger precedent. The next step is a jury trial this spring and if Apple will be able to limit the claims before then.`

data.title: Peabody evacuates workers at Wyoming mine after MSHA danger order
data.description:
Peabody Energy's Powder River Mining unit said no miners were injured after workers were evacuated from part of its North Antelope Rochelle mine in Wyoming following an MSHA imminent danger order.

Here are more details:

  • The order, issued on July 9, stemmed from concerns that loose material could fall from a highwall onto an active haul road used by mine vehicles

  • The hazard involved material that could spill over a protective berm and fall onto a roadway used by haul trucks and other vehicles, the company said in a filing

  • The company said mine personnel took measures to mitigate the hazard.

  • MSHA terminated the Section 107(a) order later the same day, according to the company

data.title: NioCorp Provides Preliminary Unaudited Financial Results for the Three-Month Period Ended September 30, 2026
data.description:
CENTENNIAL, CO / ACCESS Newswire / October 16, 2026 / NioCorp Developments Ltd. ("NioCorp," "our," or the "Company") today provided its preliminary unaudited financial results for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026, which are presented below.

The Company reported net income attributable to NioCorp of $3.7 million, or $0.03 per share (basic), for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026, as compared to a net loss attributable to NioCorp of $42.7 million, or $0.53 per share (basic), for the three months ended September 30, 2025. As of September 30, 2026, the Company had a cash balance of $405.1 million on its consolidated balance sheet.

The net income for the three months ended September 30, 2026, primarily reflects non-cash gains of approximately $8.5 million related to earnout shares and warrants classified as liabilities on the consolidated balance sheet, driven by a decrease in the closing price of the Company's common shares between June 30, 2026 and September 30, 2026. By contrast, the net loss for the three months ended September 30, 2025, primarily reflects non-cash losses of approximately $32.1 million related to earnout shares and warrants classified as liabilities on the consolidated balance sheet, driven by an increase in the closing price of the Company's common shares between June 30, 2025 and September 30, 2025.

The Company continues as a development-stage company, and its operating cash outflows for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026, totaled $6.1 million, primarily representing recurring general and administrative costs as well as costs related to the finalization and issuance of the technical and economic study related to the Elk Creek Critical Minerals Project (the "Elk Creek Project"). In addition, its investing outflows for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026, totaled $5.9 million, primarily representing additional expenditures associated with ongoing construction of the mine portal at the Elk Creek Project.

NioCorp intends to file its unaudited interim condensed consolidated financial statements for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026, in its Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q on or before November 16, 2026.

All figures reported above with respect to the three- month period ended September 30, 2026, are preliminary and are unaudited and subject to change and adjustment as the Company prepares its unaudited interim condensed consolidated financial statements for the three- month period ended September 30, 2026 and 2025. Accordingly, investors are cautioned not to place undue reliance on the foregoing information. The Company does not intend to provide preliminary results on a regular basis in the future. The preliminary results provided in this news release constitute "forward-looking information" and "forward-looking statements" within the meaning of applicable Canadian and U.S. securities laws, are based on several assumptions and are subject to a number of risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially. See "Forward-looking Statements."

# # #

NioCorp is developing the Elk Creek Project that is expected to produce niobium, scandium, titanium and several rare earth products, including neodymium-praseodymium oxide, dysprosium oxide, terbium oxide, samarium-europium-gadolinium ("SEG") carbonate, and heavy rare earth carbonate. Niobium is used to produce specialty alloys as well as High Strength, Low Alloy steel, which is a lighter, stronger steel used in automotive, structural, and pipeline applications. Scandium is a specialty metal that can be combined with Aluminum to make alloys with increased strength and improved corrosion resistance. Scandium is also a critical component of advanced solid oxide fuel cells. Titanium is used in various lightweight alloys and is a key component of pigments used in paper, paint and plastics and is also used for aerospace applications, armor, and medical implants. Magnetic rare earths, such as neodymium, praseodymium, terbium, and dysprosium are critical to the making of neodymium-iron-boron magnets, which are used across a wide variety of defense and civilian applications.

data.title: Moody's Upgrades Egypt Ratings, Citing Declining Government Debt
data.description:
By Elias Schisgall

Moody's Ratings upgraded Egypt's long-term unsecured and issuer ratings, citing the country's fiscal consolidation and reforms to reduce government debt.

The ratings agency gave long-term local and foreign-currency issuer ratings and foreign-currency senior unsecured ratings a B3 rating, up from Caa1. Moody's also gave provisional B3 ratings to the government's senior unsecured medium-term note program, as well as the unsecured MTN program of a government-owned special-purpose vehicle.

Moody's said Egypt's shift to a flexible exchange rate and tighter monetary policy has boosted the economy's resilience, and that the government has strengthened revenue collection while showing expenditure restraint.

"The government's ability to sustain this credit-positive trend despite a challenging external environment and higher oil prices highlights the durability of the improvement, rooted in increased policy effectiveness," Moody's said Friday.

Moody's also maintained a positive outlook, citing declining debt and interest burdens.

Egypt's government debt has fallen from 95.2% of gross domestic product in June 2023 to 81.8% this past June, with debt affordability also beginning to improve, Moody's said.

Write to Elias Schisgall at elias.schisgall@wsj.com

data.title: Brazil may offer credit lines to ease impact of tax, labor reforms, minister says
data.description:
Brazil's Finance Minister Dario Durigan said on Friday that specific credit lines could be unveiled by the government for companies affected by a consumer tax reform and the end of the six-day work schedule, which take effect next year.

In an interview with Band TV, Durigan added that the lines would aim to boost training, innovation, and productivity in the country.

  • Durigan spoke two days after Brazil's Senate approved a constitutional amendment to reduce the country's workweek from six days to five.

  • The new rule will take effect by the end of next year after a 14-month transition, while a consumer tax reform approved in 2023 will also take effect in 2027.

  • The minister acknowledged that some companies will be affected by the labor reform, but said he sees the impact as "minor".

  • "Business owners need government support to be part of this new era," Durigan said.

  • He also said that Brazil's high interest rates remain a problem to be tackled if President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva wins a new term in an presidential runoff later this month.

  • Lula will face Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in a second-round vote on October 25, with the leftist incumbent currently trailing the right-wing lawmaker in polls.

data.title: Cantor's $112,000 Bitcoin Call Lifts Strategy Target to $208
data.description:
Cantor Fitzgerald raised its price target on Strategy from $186 to $208 and kept an Overweight rating. The firm lifted its 12-month forward bitcoin price assumption to $112,000 from $98,000, taking a more bullish view on the asset after recent market strength. Strategy shares were down 3.32% in premarket.

Cantor values Strategy on a sum-of-the-parts basis. The firm applies 2x enterprise value to sales on Strategy's estimated 2027 sales of $509 million and values Strategy's 848,000 bitcoin at the new price assumption. That lifts its enterprise value estimate to $110 billion from $97 billion. At $112,000 each, those holdings would be worth about $95 billion.

The firm also updated its model for Strategy's latest bitcoin holdings and U.S. dollar reserves, along with a $20.91 billion gain on digital assets and a related $1.88 billion deferred tax expense.

data.title: Top News Today: Stocks Fall as CoreWeave Worries Spur AI Rout
data.description:
MARKET WRAPS

STOCKS: Stocks slid and the Nasdaq completed its largest weekly loss since June amid fears about credit costs derailing the artificial-intelligence boom.

TREASURYS: Long-term Treasury yields rose as oil prices surged again.

FOREX: The U.S. dollar fell against rivals as the upward trend in place for much of the year reversed itself this week.

COMMODITIES: Oil futures closed above the psychologically significant $100-per-barrel level in New York after the biggest weekly gain since July.

HEADLINES

Warsh Avoids Signal on October Rate Move

Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh declined to endorse or push back

on colleagues' recent signals that officials are in no rush to raise

interest rates this month, saying the central bank was no longer in the

business of previewing its decisions.

"I don't prejudge meetings. I don't believe in saying now what I might

do at the meetings we have in the balance of this year," Warsh said.

"It's a new chapter at the Fed, and we're not in that business anymore."

Warsh made the comments Friday morning local time in Bangkok in a

moderated conversation at the meetings of the International Monetary Fund

and shortly before Fed officials were set to enter their quiet period

ahead of the Oct. 27-28 meeting. He spoke with IMF Managing Director

Kristalina Georgieva.

U.S. Import Prices Rose in September

U.S. import prices rose in September for the second consecutive month,

the Bureau of Labor Statistics said Friday.

Overall import prices rose 1.1% in September, after expanding by 0.5%

in August, the BLS said. Economists polled by The Wall Street Journal had

forecast a 0.8% increase. Year-on-year import prices were up 8.1%, the

BLS said.

Import prices exclude duties, such as tariffs imposed on imports by

the Trump administration, as well as transportation costs.

From Verizon to UnitedHealth, Corporate America Is Balking at 'Tokenized'

Stocks

The country's top securities regulator made a push last month to bring

tokenized stock trading to the U.S. Now, corporate America is pushing

back.

AI chip maker Broadcom, telecom stalwart Verizon Communications and

UnitedHealth are among the companies objecting to the Securities and

Exchange Commission's plan for tokenizing their stocks, according to a

regulatory filing.

Many exchanges and trading venues are eager to offer digital tokens

that represent traditional shares and can trade 24/7. The goal is to

appeal to a class of new-age investors who have grown up on crypto and

want to trade round-the-clock. But some companies worry the SEC's plan

for tokenization might create a shadow stock market, distort trading and

confuse investors.

Travelers Profit Ticks Up on Investment Gains

Travelers reported higher quarterly profit, despite roughly flat

revenue, helped by investment gains.

The insurance company on Friday posted a third-quarter profit of $1.92

billion, or $9.04 a share, compared with $1.89 billion, or $8.24 a share,

a year earlier.

Core earnings per share were $9.18, compared with analyst estimates of

$7.39, according to FactSet.

Regions Financial Posts Higher Profit, Revenue

Regions Financial posted higher profit and revenue in the third

quarter, as both net interest income and non-interest income grew.

The Regions Bank parent posted a profit of $611 million, or 71 cents a

share, compared with $539 million, or 62 cents a share, in the same

quarter a year earlier.

Stripping out one-time items, earnings came in at 73 cents a share.

Analysts polled by FactSet had expected adjusted earnings of 66 cents a

share.

The U.S. budget deficit just hit almost $2 trillion - and Washington

isn't doing much about it

The U.S. federal government's annual budget deficit reached almost $2

trillion for the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30, the Treasury Department

said Friday.

The deficit figure of $1.992 trillion is the largest since 2021 and

amounts to an estimated 6.2% of U.S. gross domestic product, according to

Treasury officials.

It represents a fresh sign of Washington's tendency to spend much more

than it takes in even when the U.S. economy isn't in a recession, and

comes just a couple of months after a bout of hand-wringing over the

government's total debt surpassing $40 trillion.

Cleveland-Cliffs Braces for Fight as Canada Looks to Block Layoffs at

Stelco

OTTAWA-Cleveland-Cliffs is digging in on planned lay offs at its

Stelco operations in Canada as Prime Minister Mark Carney's government

weighs legal options, including fines and potentially forced sale of

assets, to protect workers.

Calls for Ottawa to take action have grown in recent days after Stelco

began handing out layoff notices. Industry Minister Melanie Joly had

earlier requested that the steel company produce a plan to comply with

promises on jobs she said were agreed to when Cliffs bought Stelco in

2024 for about $2.5 billion.

Cliffs Chief Executive Lourenco Goncalves said the company hasn't

breached the law and that a temporary reduction in headcount is needed as

it refocuses its operations to counter the pressure on the industry from

tariffs. The company, which is set to report quarterly results on Monday,

said it could lay off as many as 500 workers as it idles cold-rolled and

coated steel operations in Hamilton, Ontario, and concentrates on

hot-roll products.

Tesla's New Roadster Takes Flight After Nearly a Decade of Delays

After nine years, potentially millions of dollars in deposits and

considerable hype, the Tesla Roadster is finally ready to launch-which it

did.

The electric automaker on Thursday unveiled its second-generation

sports car with a flourish of engineering prowess. Using SpaceX rocket

technology, the angular sports car climbed a curved ramp and hurled

itself to a controlled landing. Later, it leapt over five other Tesla

vehicles while twisting in the air.

The demonstration was held before a crowd of Tesla enthusiasts-some of

whom paid $250,000 to reserve the car nine years ago-at a SpaceX rocket

test site facility in McGregor, Texas.

Tesla's Energy Boss Leaves the Company

Tesla's top energy boss has left the company.

Mike Snyder, vice president of energy and charging, stepped down from

his role, according to people familiar with the move.

Snyder joined Tesla in 2014 and worked his way up to lead the

company's Megapack industrial battery division, according to his LinkedIn

page. He was promoted to vice president in 2024 following a companywide

restructuring and layoffs that saw the departure of several of Tesla's

top executives, including longtime energy chief Drew Baglino.

TALKING POINT Michael Dell, a Dot-Com Era Survivor, Has Tips to Beat an AI Bust

Spooked investors are fleeing some of the big-tech companies that reached new highs on the back of the artificial-intelligence boom.

But Michael Dell says his company is well-placed to weather a storm. The direct-to-consumer PC company he founded in a dorm room in 1984 with $1,000 has pivoted to delivering the powerful supercomputers that tech giants can't get enough of. And its strategy for selling them makes it relatively unique among the businesses benefiting most from the world's unprecedented AI infrastructure build-out.

Dell relies on just-in-time manufacturing of its AI servers and PCs, which has allowed it, in essence, to get its customers to finance its operations and inventory. Meanwhile, hyperscalers like Amazon.com and Google and the builders of their AI data centers-the so-called neoclouds like CoreWeave, Nebius and Crusoe-are piling on debt to fund the build-out of their AI hubs.

Dell Technologies' valuation is almost four times what it was a year ago, boosted by a projected 70% increase in revenue for its current fiscal year.

When I asked Dell on Tuesday about how he was preparing his company for a possible downturn in the AI cycle, he said, "There are some new challenges that this presents, but if you look at our cash conversion cycle, it's still negative."

data.title: Microsoft Makes a Massive Move to Secure Its AI Future
data.description:
NiSource shares rose after the utility signed a 20-year energy agreement with Microsoft to supply roughly 1,100 megawatts of new generation capacity beginning in 2028.

The deal is another sign of just how much power Big Tech is securing for future data-center expansion.

Under the agreement, NiSource's NIPSCO and GenCo units will provide the generation and transmission infrastructure needed to serve Microsoft's load while continuing to support existing customers in Indiana.

Microsoft will fully fund the generation and transmission assets required for its data-center demand, according to the companies.

That point matters because utilities across the U.S. are facing growing scrutiny over whether residential customers could end up subsidizing infrastructure built for hyperscale data centers.

NiSource says that will not happen here.

The new assets are also expected to strengthen NIPSCO's transmission system, improving grid reliability and resilience for existing customers.

The agreement includes another major component: 600 MW of battery storage under a long-term tolling agreement with GenCo. The storage facility will be developed and constructed by an affiliate of AGP Group.

NiSource said the Microsoft agreement increases expected savings for NIPSCO electric customers over the life of its data-center contracts to about $1.75 billion, up from the previously disclosed $1.4 billion.

That could equate to savings of as much as $140 per customer annually.

Shares of NiSource gained roughly 3% in early Friday trading following the announcement.

Investor Takeaway

I think the more important part of this deal is not simply the 1,100 MW headline.

It is the contract structure.

Microsoft is effectively underwriting the infrastructure required for its own demand, while NiSource gains a very large, long-duration customer without shifting the capital burden onto existing ratepayers.

That could make the agreement a useful template for utilities trying to capture AI-driven electricity demand without creating political or regulatory backlash.

For investors, the key things to watch are project execution, regulatory approvals, returns on invested capital, transmission expansion and whether NiSource signs additional hyperscaler agreements.

If more data-center customers are willing to directly fund the infrastructure they require, AI-related load growth could become a much cleaner earnings opportunity for regulated utilities.

data.title: Foreign US Treasury holdings rise in August, but China cuts to 2008 low
data.description:
Foreign holdings of US Treasuries edged higher in August after two months of declines, data from the Treasury Department showed on Friday, led by gains in holdings from the UK and Canada.

Holdings of US Treasuries rose to $9.331 trillion in August, from $9.248 trillion in the previous month. They hit a record $9.487 trillion in February this year. Compared with a year earlier, Treasuries owned by foreigners were up less than 1%.

China's holdings, however, dropped to their lowest since August 2008.

Here are some details:

* Holdings from Japan fell to $1.068 trillion in August, down 3.2% from $1.103 trillion in July. These holdings dropped for a fourth straight month. Japan, however, remained the largest non-US holder of Treasuries, with holdings hitting a peak of $1.325 trillion in November 2021.

* Holdings from the United Kingdom, the second-largest foreign holder of Treasuries, topped the trillion-dollar mark for the first time. The UK posted a 1.1% increase in holdings to $1.009 trillion in August, from $998.3 billion the previous month. The UK is widely viewed as a major custody hub for global investors, and its flows are often considered a proxy for hedge fund capital.

* China's hoard of Treasuries dropped 2.4% to $590.7 billion in August, from $618 billion in July, falling for the third consecutive month. China's holdings in August were the lowest since August 2008, when these declined to $573.7 billion.

* China is still the third-largest non-US holder of Treasuries. Its August holdings have fallen by nearly 16% from levels a year earlier.

* Canada, the fifth-largest owner of Treasuries, raised its holdings to $490.5 billion, up 4.2% from a month earlier.

* On a transaction basis, August saw a large Treasury inflow of $108.9 billion, from an outflow of $3.6 billion in July.

* US corporate bonds posted inflows of $41.6 billion in August, compared with inflows of $26.9 billion in July.

* US equity inflows surged to $153.9 billion in August, up from inflows of $3.7 billion the previous month.

* Overall net capital inflows for August increased to $199.8 billion, up from $87.4 billion in July.

The rules of the SEC require that when a registrant prepares, on or after the date a registrant reports an accounting change such as the change in segment reporting described above, a new registration, proxy, or information statement (or amends a previously filed registration, proxy, or information statement) that includes or incorporates by reference financial statements, the registrant must recast the prior period financial statements included or incorporated by reference in the registration, proxy, or information statement to reflect these types of changes. Included within Exhibit 99.1 to this Form 8-K and incorporated herein are the following items from the 2025 Form 10-K, each recast to reflect the impact of the Company's change in business segments on the Company's consolidated financial information and certain related disclosures:

data.title: BUUU Group Plans 10-for-1 Forward Share Split

BUUU Group said its board approved a 10-for-1 forward stock split, which will see the company's Class A and Class B ordinary shares be split into 10 shares each of the same class.

The Company intends to use the net proceeds of the Offering for working capital requirements and general corporate purposes. The Units were offered to purchasers in reliance on available prospectus exemptions under applicable Canadian securities laws.

Offering Terms

Each Unit consists of one common share in the capital of the Company (each, a "Common Share") and one Common Share purchase warrant (each, a "Warrant"). Each Warrant entitles the holder thereof to purchase one additional Common Share at a price of C$0.10 until October 16, 2028; provided, however, that if, at any time prior to the expiry of the Warrants, the closing price of the Common Shares on the Canadian Securities Exchange (the "CSE") equals or exceeds C$0.15 per Common Share for a period of 10 consecutive trading days, the Company may, at its option, accelerate the expiry date of the Warrants by giving written notice to the holders thereof, and in such case, the Warrants will expire on the 30th day after the date on which such notice is given by the Company. All securities issued in connection with the First Tranche are subject to a statutory hold period expiring February 17, 2027, in accordance with applicable securities legislation.

The Company anticipates closing one or more subsequent tranches of the Offering.

data.title: FAA poised to approve Boeing 737 MAX 10 as soon as next week - Reuters
data.description:
The Federal Aviation Administration ‌is set to approve the long-delayed Boeing 737 MAX 10 as soon as next week after completing a key safety review, Reuters reported Friday.

In one of the last steps prior to final approval, the FAA and Boeing reportedly held a successful meeting Friday of the Type Certification Board, which is comprised of agency management team members.

Airlines have ordered nearly 1,500 MAX 10s, and the model accounts for ~30% of Boeing's outstanding ​737 backlog, but numerous delays have helped European rival Airbus' A321neo secure a greater share of the large single-aisle market.

A glitch with the latest update ​of the 737 ⁠MAX's navigation software threatened to further delay certification when Boeing disclosed it last month, but the FAA determined it did not pose a safety concern and did not require a fix as ​a condition of certifying the plane.

Boeing is still working on certifying ​the 777-9, its largest jetliner in production and six years behind schedule.

By Elias Schisgall

Hyperscale Data's artificial-intelligence technology subsidiary, askROI, plans to go public in the second or third quarter of next year.

The AI data center company said askROI may go public through an initial public offering, reverse takeover, or merger with a special purpose acquisition company.

As part of the planned deal, Hyperscale Data Executive Chairman Milton "Todd" Ault III will step down as chief executive of askROI. The subsidiary is expected to appoint Joseph Spaziano as CEO and Ryan Doucette as president, and Hyperscale Data added that it anticipates both will stay on once askROI goes public.

Spaziano currently serves as president and chief operating officer of askROI and chief technology officer of the parent company. He is expected to step down from the latter role to focus entirely on askROI.

Hyperscale Data said the move builds on its strategy of positioning its operating businesses for independent growth and separate market valuations.

data.title: Stocks slip as dollar heads for weekly loss
data.description:
Key points:
  • US dollar heads for weekly loss on lower US Treasury yields
  • Bond markets stabilize after rush for safe havens on Thursday
  • Investors worry about debt risks in AI-related stocks

By Chibuike Oguh and Elizabeth Howcroft

Global stocks fell modestly on Friday as markets stabilized after a sharp tech-led selloff, while the dollar headed for a weekly loss.

Markets have been rattled this week by concerns over higher interest rates and the debt-fuelled financing behind the AI boom, triggering a selloff in technology and chip stocks.

Traders increased bets on further US rate hikes after stronger-than-expected inflation data was released on Wednesday, while investors piled in to Treasuries and other government bonds.

On Wall Street, the benchmark S&P 500 and the Nasdaq finished down and notched weekly losses. The Dow fell as well after reversing early gains but still scored a weekly gain.

Technology and communication services drove losses while the top gainers were utilities and energy stocks.

CoreWeave's shares shed 12% and lost about 25% this week amid increasing investor scrutiny of the financing for the massive AI infrastructure buildout.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.34%, the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX lost 1.09%, and the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.1%.

The MSCI World Equity Index lost 0.40% and notched a weekly loss EURONEXT:IACWI.

European stock indexes, hit less hard by Thursday's selloff, gained, with the STOXX 600 adding 0.72% . London's FTSE 100 CURRENCYCOM:UK100 rose 0.38%. Both indexes finished the week higher.

"We're starting to see some cracks in the financing of data centers because you're not too sure who's going to be the winners," said Tom Plumb, portfolio manager at Plumb Balanced Fund.

"Our view is that there's going to be some really significant winners," he said. "But you have to be careful on the financing capability because companies don't get into trouble because their assets don't exceed their liabilities. They get into trouble when they have liquidity issues."

Asian stocks mostly rose, and bond markets steadied, with investors reversing some of the previous session's moves.

Indonesian equities suffered their biggest drop since 1998 after index provider MSCI said the country's market no longer merited emerging-market status and outlined plans to remove it from key indexes tracked by funds.

DOLLAR FALLS

The dollar index fell 0.26% and was on track for its first weekly decline after four weeks of gains, as lower Treasury yields reduced the currency's appeal. Further worries about AI would push the dollar down further, analysts said.

The euro rose from its recent 17-month low. It was last up 0.16% at $1.1238 .

The Japanese yen rose 0.01% against the greenback to 157.98 per dollar.

European government bond yields edged higher, while US bond yields reversed earlier declines. Germany's 10-year yield rose 1.14 basis points to 3.421% (DE10YT=RR). The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes rose 0.17 basis points to 5.085%.

Even so, yields have eased this week as investors sought the safety of government debt amid concerns about AI-related companies' finances. G7 government bond markets were on course for their strongest weekly performance since late May.

Brent crude futures rose 3.72% to settle at $109.86 a barrel and were headed for a second straight weekly gain amid concerns over Middle East supplies. Attacks around the Strait of Hormuz have surged in the past 10 days.

Gold (XAU) gained support from the weaker dollar, rising 0.07% to $4,167.14 an ounce.

data.title: Pacific Imperial Announces Private Placement Cancellation Due to Re-Pricing Requirement
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

Vancouver, British Columbia – October 16, 2026 – TheNewswire - Pacific Imperial Mines Inc. (TSX.V: PPM) (“Pacific Imperial” or the “Company”) announces that it is cancelling its proposed private placement (the “Private Placement”) of flow-through units and non-flow-through units, as previously described in the Company’s press release dated September 9, 2026. After an internal review conducted by the TSX Venture Exchange (the “TSXV”) completed on October 15, 2026, the TSXV determined that the closing price of $0.10 (after adjusting for the consolidation), which was used to establish the issue price of $0.075 for the Private Placement, was not a fair reflection of the market price for the Company’s common shares, and confirmed that the Company would need to reprice the Private Placement.

The TSXV advised the Company on October 8th that the reserve price established was not a fair reflection of the market price for the Company’s common shares and the offering would need to be repriced. The Company advised the TSXV on October 9th that the re-pricing would be unacceptable to the committed subscribers.

The Company thoroughly reviewed its strategic options and confirmed that a mandate to reprice the Private Placement would cause existing subscribers to withdraw their commitments from the Private Placement. Accordingly, the Company has decided to formally cancel the proposed Private Placement and will be re-evaluating how to move forward.

Pacific Imperial is a mineral exploration company based in Vancouver, Canada, engaged in the acquisition, exploration, evaluation and development of mineral properties in an acceptable risk environment. data.title: Emerging Growth Research Publishes Update on Newton Golf’s Pole Canyon Option and Critical Minerals Strategy
data.description:
NEW YORK CITY, NY / ACCESS Newswire / October 16, 2026 / Emerging Growth Research ("EGR") today announced the publication of a company-sponsored Flash Report covering Newton Golf Company, Inc. , a technology-focused golf equipment company that develops and sells premium golf shafts, putters and related products.

The report examines Newton Golf's recently announced option to acquire the Pole Canyon project, a historic beryllium-tungsten property located in White Pine County, Nevada. It also discusses the Company's move into the U.S. critical minerals sector and the effect of the associated share issuance on EGR's earnings-per-share estimates.

Key Highlights

  • Pole Canyon Option - On September 24, 2026, Newton Golf announced it had completed a transaction granting it an option to acquire the Pole Canyon project, a historic beryllium-tungsten property in White Pine County, Nevada. The transaction represents the Company's entry into the U.S. critical minerals sector.
  • Consideration - In connection with the option, Newton Golf issued shares equal to 19.9% of its issued and outstanding common stock. Using EGR's previous estimate of shares outstanding at the end of Q3:26, the issuance is estimated at approximately 1.13 million shares.
  • Critical Minerals - Beryllium appears on the U.S. Geological Survey's 2025 List of Critical Minerals, while tungsten is included on the U.S. Department of Energy's 2023 Final Critical Materials List. Both materials have applications in aerospace, defense and advanced manufacturing.
  • Project Overview - Pole Canyon is a past-producing property comprising 16 unpatented lode claims across approximately 330 acres, about 50 miles southeast of Ely, Nevada. Historical materials describe a mineralized system extending for more than 4,000 feet and reportedly open along strike and at depth. They also cite a historical estimate of approximately 281,725 tons grading 0.75% beryllium oxide and 0.30% tungsten trioxide. Newton Golf has not independently verified these historical estimates.
  • Strategy - Newton Golf has stated that it does not plan to begin mining operations at this time. The Company instead intends to consider potential strategic agreements, with the option structure providing exposure to the project while limiting near-term operating and capital commitments.
  • Estimate Updates - EGR does not expect the transaction to affect the Company's revenue or operating income and has not changed its revenue forecasts. Reflecting the additional shares outstanding, EGR's FY:26 loss-per-share estimate narrows to $(1.23) from $(1.37), and its FY:27 estimate narrows to $(0.38) from $(0.42).
  • Risks - Newton Golf continues to generate negative cash flow and may need to obtain additional capital to support its growth plans. Demand for its products may be affected by shifts in consumer preferences and sentiment, as golf equipment is discretionary. The Pole Canyon option is at an early stage, mining is not currently underway, and there can be no assurance the project will generate value for the Company.

Newton Golf sells its products through direct-to-consumer channels, professional club fitters, distributors, golf retailers and other channels, with distribution primarily in the United States and additional international markets including Japan and South Korea.

data.title: ATLANTIC AMERICAN CORP FY 2025: Revenue $210.4M, EPS $0.28— 10-K Summary
data.description:
Atlantic American Corp reported fiscal 2025 revenue of $210.4M and net income of $6.02M, or diluted EPS of $0.28, reversing a net loss in 2024 as underwriting improvements, higher premiums and investment gains supported profitability.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue was $210.4M, compared with $188.1M in the prior year; YoY change 11.9%.
  • Net income was $6.02M, compared with $(1.39M) in the prior year.
  • Diluted EPS was $0.28, compared with $(0.09) in the prior year.

Business Highlights

  • Consolidated revenue rose to $210.4M from $188.1M, driven by higher property & casualty and Medicare Supplement premiums.
  • Auto liability rate increases and new inland marine programs boosted P&C writings.
  • Medicare Supplement new sales increased in the life & health segment, supporting growth.
  • Underwriting performance improved: American Southern’s combined ratio improved to 99.1% from 105.4%, and Bankers Fidelity maintained a 97.5% combined ratio.
  • The company identified a material weakness in premium receivable controls, restated 2024 figures and has implemented remediation steps to strengthen reconciliations.
  • Net investment income rose and equity unrealized gains contributed to 2025 profitability alongside increased earned premiums.

Original SEC Filing: ATLANTIC AMERICAN CORP [ AAME ] - 10-K - Oct. 16, 2026
